verdict: The design is sound but not ready to build. One blocker and twelve majors must be fixed first. Storage option (a) is the right choice: nothing is persisted, the draft is held in memory and the page locks in place. The claims hold that no migration is needed and that no #42 file is touched: the audit action is free text, end_reason 'signed_out' is allowed, tp_app holds UPDATE(ended_at, end_reason), and proxy.ts, next.config.ts, app/layout.tsx, sign-in.ts and pending.ts are not in the #42 list. Several other claims were also checked and hold: all 105 runAction call sites pass practiceId and only under app/p; FormKeys renders value= so router.refresh re-keys the forms; the loading.tsx files under /p stop prefetch at the layout. What fails: the planned onSubmit rewrite of the forms can put PHI in a URL. ADR 0072 is already taken by #38. The touch route breaks the generated route tests. The Clear-Site-Data header needs owner consent that the design gives itself. There are several paths it misses where a narrative is still lost (network error, maintenance or terms redirect, a refresh at the 12-hour end, mobile tab discard). Three of its claims are false: the clock 'never locks late', 'another user's sign-in clears the draft', and 'nothing persisted' (form-state restore). The reviewer progress notes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/cd4c3776-ffb4-50ed-99cf-e6bf837d5699/scratchpad/nd-design/progress/reviewer.md.

findings.finding: Section 4.9 / N10: moving ActionForm (and VersionForm) to onSubmit with preventDefault and startTransition, without keeping a function action, makes a form submitted before hydration (or with script failed) fall back to a native GET to the current URL. That GET puts the narrative, case notes and other typed PHI in the query string, browser history and server logs (CLAUDE.md: never PHI in a URL).
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/components/action-form.tsx:69 (today `<form action={formAction}>`, which React keeps safe before hydration); version-form.tsx:120 (`<form action={writeDispatch}>`); design lines 480-484
findings.fix: Keep `action={formAction}` on the form, add `method="post"`, and add the onSubmit handler on top: it calls preventDefault and dispatches without the reset. Before hydration React still queues the action and never issues a GET. Add a unit or static check that every form under /p has method post or a function action, and an e2e case with JavaScript disabled that asserts the URL holds no typed word.

findings.finding: The ADR number collides. #38's design takes ADR 0072, and LANES.md gives 0073 to bank-account-first. The narrative design still names 0072 in its title, file name, section 9, N17, sessions.md and the reconciliation sub-bullet. Its claim that the #38 design 'did not exist at design time' is now out of date. The CAS IDs are fine: #38 takes CAS-30 to CAS-34 and leaves CAS-35 to CAS-37.
findings.evidence: /home/user/ops/designs/lane-b-figures-in-words.md:7-10 ('This PR takes ADR 0072 and CAS-30 to CAS-34. It leaves CAS-35 to CAS-37 to #48 ... takes the next free number'); /home/user/ops/LANES.md:173 (ADR 0073 to bank-account-first); design lines 62, 827, 844-853
findings.fix: Take the next ADR number free in LANES.md (0074 unless already claimed) and have the orchestrator record it in line 172's claim. Rename every reference together and drop the 'did not exist' sentence.

findings.finding: The touch route's `if (request.fetchSite !== 'same-origin') throw new NotFoundError()` breaks the generated per-route tests. Their harness sends no Sec-Fetch-Site, so every persona test gets not_found where the persona matrix expects ok. The design's 'gets the generated SEC-15 tests ... with no edit' is false. The check also runs after signedIn(), so it does not stop a cross-site navigation from renewing the session.
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/routes/route-tests/world.ts:606-627 (fetchSite set only for cross-site); define.ts:96-101 (expects the persona-matrix status); lib/http/invoke.ts:425-432 (signedIn before handle); design lines 249-252, 747-748
findings.fix: Refuse only when the header is present and is not same-origin, as sameOrigin() does (csrf.ts:52-59): `if (request.fetchSite != null && request.fetchSite !== 'same-origin' && request.fetchSite !== 'none')`. Or drop the check: the body holds nothing secret, CORS blocks cross-origin reads, and SameSite=Lax already keeps subresource requests from carrying the cookie. Correct the ADR text: the check does not prevent the touch.

findings.finding: Adding Clear-Site-Data is a change to the security headers, and the reconciliation check says such a change needs the owner's consent. The design writes a 'Ruled by the co-founder' sub-bullet into reconciliation-001 based only on the blanket safer-option ruling. Under option (a) the header buys almost nothing: nothing is stored, PHI pages are no-store, and the bfcache case is handled by pageshow. A cross-site link to /sign-in?reason=signed_out also clears the HTTP cache, because headers() cannot apply the design's gate.
findings.evidence: docs/product/reconciliation-001.md:300 ('Every option changes the security program, so each needs your consent'), :472, :440 ('A pull request that cannot pass one stops and asks the owner'); next.config.ts:24; design lines 560-564, 832-837
findings.fix: Drop Clear-Site-Data, so no header changes and no ruling is needed. Rely on the hard reload, the pageshow and pagehide handling and the e2e checks that storage is empty. If it is kept, put it to the owner as a question rather than recording a ruling, and add `missing: [{type:'cookie', key:'tp_session'}]` to the rule.

findings.finding: Sign-in completes by a server-action redirect, which is a soft navigation. In one tab, A's JavaScript heap and Next's router cache (A's /p pages) survive into B's session. If B signs in in the tab A left, Back can restore A's cached PHI page with no request. The beacon is mounted by the root layout on a full load, so a hello for B's marker may never be sent, and the claim that other tabs lock 'at once, on whatever page B lands' rests on that hello. The hard reload is planned only for reason=signed_out, not for idle, ended or expired.
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/http/next.ts:197-199 (redirect in runSignInStep); app/sign-in/actions.ts:8-23; components/hardware-key.tsx:57,111 (only the key path does a full load); design lines 536-539, 552-559
findings.fix: Make every settle() signed_in end in a full document load: after sign-in, land on a tiny page that calls location.replace(next or '/'), or switch the client to location.assign. Run <SignedOut />'s 'hard reload if reached by soft navigation' on every /sign-in landing, whatever the reason. Have the beacon broadcast on mount and whenever its marker prop changes. Add an e2e case: A is idle on /p, the redirect lands on sign-in, B signs in in the same tab, presses Back twice, and no A text appears.

findings.finding: The clock's starting points break its 'never locks late' guarantee. (1) `lastContact = performance.timeOrigin` is the document's start, but the /p layout often mounts on a soft navigation from /, /settings or /console. In a document hours old, the guard locks at once (a false lock). (2) Counting a pathname change as contact is wrong when Back or Forward is served from the router cache with no request, which happens with the browser's own Back button, a press the document never sees as input. The guard then believes there was contact while the server's idle clock keeps running, so the page can stay readable up to 30 minutes past the server's end, which is what the audit fails. (3) With page.clock installed, timeOrigin is real while Date is fake, so the e2e is flaky.
findings.evidence: design lines 286-291, 357; app/p/**/loading.tsx (soft navigations into /p); app/layout.tsx (no /p layout today)
findings.fix: Count only contacts actually observed: a touch answered, a server-action result, and RSC or fetch responses seen through a PerformanceObserver on resource entries (same-origin `_rsc` or route requests). A pathname change is not contact. At mount, set lastContact to Date.now() minus a margin, or to a server `renderedAt` passed by the layout and adjusted for skew. Use Date.now() everywhere. Add property-test events for 'navigation from cache, no request' and 'mount by soft navigation in an old document'.

findings.finding: Network loss or a server error on save loses the narrative. A server action that rejects (offline, a 502 from the load balancer, a 500) throws into the transition, and with useActionState the error goes to app/error.tsx, the root error boundary. That unmounts the whole tree, guard and narrative copy included. The orchestrator listed network loss; the design does not cover it.
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/app/error.tsx (the only error boundary, at the root); version-form.tsx:97-98, action-form.tsx:31 (useActionState dispatch)
findings.fix: Inside the guard, wrap each form's action in a client wrapper: `async (s, f) => { try { return await action(s, f); } catch { return { error: NOT_SENT_MESSAGE } } }`, re-throwing only Next's redirect and notFound signals. The text stays and the person retries. Add an error.tsx under app/p/[practiceId] that sits below the guard, so the copy survives a render error. Add an e2e case that aborts the action request with page.route and checks the text is still there.

findings.finding: Practice actions still redirect on maintenance, terms_required, mfa_required and hardware_key_required, so a save while maintenance starts or new terms are published still loses the text. Section 4.9 keeps these redirects on purpose.
findings.fix: For practice actions, return a non-navigating state for every redirecting status, for example `{ session: 'blocked', blockedBy: 'maintenance' | 'terms' | 'mfa' }`. Lock or notice in place with a link that opens /maintenance, /terms or the MFA step in a new tab, and keep the text. Add an e2e case: maintenance switched on while typing, then save, then the text is still there.

findings.finding: A router.refresh() near or after the 12-hour end, or after any server-side end the guard has not seen, re-renders through loadPage. That redirects to sign-in and navigates away, losing the narrative. ExportStatus refreshes every 5 seconds while attended, and the uploader refreshes on settledAll. Pausing only when unattended does not cover a person working through the hard limit.
findings.fix: useAttended() should also return false once phase is not active and from endsAt minus 60 seconds. Run the restore's own refresh only after a 200 touch, as designed. Have polls call the touch route first, or call refresh only after a successful fetch of a lightweight route, so a 401 locks instead of navigating. Add an e2e case: a live export with expires_at moved to now, then the page locks and the text survives.

findings.finding: `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener')` always returns null by spec, so 'if it returns null, show an ordinary link' always fires and cannot tell a blocked popup from a tab that opened. window.close() in /sign-in/resumed is also unreliable: after several sign-in steps the new tab's history has more than one entry, so most browsers will not let script close it.
findings.fix: Make 'Sign in again' an `<a href target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">` with visible text '(opens a new tab)': it is never blocked and is announced properly. Treat window.close() as best effort; the resumed page's wording already covers it staying open.

findings.finding: The claim that nothing is ever written anywhere is not proven against the browser's own form-state and session restore. Chromium stores each page's form-control state in its session history and writes it to the profile's Sessions files, which restore tabs after a crash or restart, while the person types. The design adds autoComplete=off only to the narrative textarea. The case note, line note, payer-response notes, reasons and contract answers on /p pages are uncontrolled fields with no such attribute. The 12-hour hold makes this worse, since a locked tab's form state is on disk overnight. (Plausible: the browser internals are recalled, not tested here.)
findings.evidence: design lines 530-531, 606-616; components/action-form.tsx:69 (no autoComplete); grep shows autoComplete=off only on reference-search and screening fields
findings.fix: Inside the guard, render `autoComplete="off"` on every form, which covers its controls, and also on the textareas. Record in the ADR that browsers may still persist session-restore data, and that this is outside the product's control. Add a static test that every form under /p carries autoComplete off. Raise improvement 7 (spellcheck=false) to the same decision, since both send or keep typed PHI outside the page.

findings.finding: The claims 'Cleared on another user's sign-in: Yes' and CAS-37's 'drops its unsaved text' are false until someone presses Continue in that tab. On hello with a different marker the tab only locks with reason 'changed'. It cannot tell the same user from another, so A's text stays in that tab's memory and DOM for up to 12 hours while B uses the browser.
findings.fix: Add an opaque user marker to the hello and view cookie (HMAC of userId under a purpose of its own, never the ID). A tab that hears a different user marker drops the copy and calls location.replace at once, with no request. A same-user change keeps the lock-and-Continue path. Update CAS-37's e2e so it asserts the text has left the DOM before any click.

findings.finding: Restoring through a second tab is fragile on the supported phone width and for assistive technology. iOS Safari and Android Chrome often discard a background tab while the person signs in elsewhere, which loses the draft the design means to keep (section 15 accepts this). Juggling tabs also makes screen-reader users switch context (the 'Go back to the tab you were working in' wording).
findings.fix: Offer re-authentication in place: an in-page dialog that runs the existing sign-in step routes (password, TOTP, hardware key through WebAuthn, which works in-page). Use variants that return the next step instead of redirecting, so the tab never unloads. Keep the new-tab path as a fallback for steps that need a full page (new password, enrollment). If the build cannot do this now, record the in-place dialog in the ADR's 'Revisit when' and make the risk explicit in the PR.

findings.finding: Tests are missing for the paths above and for some claims the design states.
findings.fix: Add: (1) pre-hydration or no-JS submit, with no typed word in any URL; (2) save with the network aborted; (3) maintenance or terms switched on mid-typing; (4) a live export at the 12-hour end; (5) a same-tab sign-in by a different user, then Back; (6) the guard mounted by soft navigation in an old document (no false lock); (7) Back served from cache after idle (no late lock); (8) a hello from a different user drops the text before any click; (9) the generated route tests and registry.test.ts passing with the new route and page; (10) a static check that /p forms carry autoComplete off; (11) the guard's own reloads (sign-out broadcast, other user, 12-hour hold) are not blocked by its beforeunload handler.

findings.finding: The new page app/sign-in/resumed/page.tsx needs a registered public page route at /sign-in/resumed, added to SIGN_IN_ROUTES and loaded with loadPublicPage. Otherwise registry.test.ts fails. The design does not mention it.
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/routes/registry.test.ts:135-148 ('runs every page through a registered page route at its own path'); design lines 193, 885
findings.fix: Add `signedInAgainPage = publicRoute({ id: 'sign_in.resumed', kind: 'page', path: '/sign-in/resumed', ... })` to sign-in.ts, with no #42 file. Gate its signed_in broadcast on Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin plus a one-time flag set by settle(), so a visit from another site does not make locked tabs send an automatic touch.

findings.finding: The response handling is keyed on the wrong HTTP status. mfa_required and hardware_key_required come back as 401, not 403. 429 (a rate limit on the mutation bucket) is not handled at all.
findings.fix: Branch on the JSON body's `status` and `reason`, not on the HTTP code. Treat 429 as 'try again at the next activity', without locking.

findings.finding: With the trailing touch, the screen can stay readable up to 35 minutes after the last input: the last touch comes up to 5 minutes after the last activity, and the lock is 30 minutes after that touch. The warning's words 'signed out after 30 minutes without activity', and sessions.md:19, then overstate it.
findings.fix: Lock on the client at min(lastContact, lastActivity) plus 30 minutes, which is never later than the server. Or state the bound in the ADR and sessions.md ('the server ends a session 30 minutes after its last request; the screen locks 30 minutes after the last input').

findings.finding: The guard's own programmatic reloads (another tab's signed_out, another user's Continue, the 12-hour draft hold) run while a form is dirty. Its beforeunload handler will prompt and can block them. Background tabs also suppress the prompt inconsistently.
findings.fix: Before any intentional reload, hide the page, drop the copy and remove the beforeunload handler. If the navigation is still blocked or cancelled, the tab stays locked.

findings.finding: resolve_session reports device_revoked or user_disabled only to the first request after the event. Later requests, and an admin's revoke-all, report 'ended', and an idle check comes before the revocation check. Whether the draft is dropped (section 4.9) therefore depends on which tab or poll resolved first.
findings.fix: State in the ADR that dropping on revocation is best effort and bounded by DRAFT_HOLD_MS. Optionally, the touch route can read end_reason for the caller's own ended session (RLS self policy) and report 'revoked'.

findings.finding: A restored bfcache page or a waking laptop can paint the old frame before pageshow or the timer runs, so PHI is briefly readable. The same-user hello from /sign-in/resumed can lock an active tab for a moment (reason changed) before signed_in restores it, which contradicts 'with no lock' at line 441.
findings.fix: On pagehide set the hidden lock state, so a page restored from bfcache stays hidden until the guard decides. Process signed_in before the hello from the same page, or ignore a hello whose marker equals a pending signed_in. Correct the wording.

findings.finding: lib/session/return-path.ts imports ROUTES from lib/routes/index.ts, which pulls in server and database code. If the lock screen's client code imports it to build `next`, the client bundle takes in server modules.
findings.fix: Keep returnPath server-only (`import 'server-only'`). The client sends location.pathname unvalidated, and the sign-in page and password step validate it. Consider carrying next and resume inside the existing sealed Pending cookie instead of a new tp_return cookie (pending.ts:22-25): one less cookie, and the same lifetime as the step.

findings.finding: The WCAG wording overreaches. Citing 2.2.1's essential exception for a 12-hour security limit is arguable. W3C's understanding note does not treat security as automatically essential, and 2.2.1 also has its own 20-hour exception, which 12 hours does not meet.
findings.fix: In the ADR, ground the 12-hour behaviour in the advance notice plus re-authentication that loses nothing (2.2.5), and record the essential-exception reading as a judgment, not as compliance.

findings.finding: endReplacedSession records the replaced session's end as end_reason 'signed_out', which merges deliberate sign-outs with replacements in the session record (the CHECK has no 'replaced' value, and adding one would need a migration).
findings.fix: Keep 'signed_out', since no migration is allowed. Put `purpose: 'replaced'` on the session_replaced audit event so the access log can tell them apart. Say this in the ADR.
